Definition: something given as security, i.e. (literally) a token (of safety) or (metaphorically) a bondsman
BiblicalUsage: The pledge is a token left as security, and it is used twice. Jesse sends his son to the camp with ten cheeses for the captain and a pledge from his brothers, that he may know how they fare; and the proverb warns that a man void of understanding striketh hands and becometh surety for his friend.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for a pledge carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the lesson, that a token given in trust is a serious thing, and standing surety for another man is not to be done lightly.
